- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high or use 2-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not drop below 1–2% below recent low.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overreact to sentiment swings; use sentiment-weighted average of last 7–10 days to anchor forecast, not full sentiment history.
- If sentiment peaks early in forecast horizon (e.g., day 1–3), model often overcorrects; dampen initial forecast by 2–5% to avoid premature rally.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5), model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 3-period smoothing or ignore sentiment if >2 consecutive days are extreme.
